points.quote: The University currently endorses the use of Microsoft CoPilot and Adobe Firefly.
points.gist: The University endorses Microsoft CoPilot and Adobe Firefly.

points.quote: In line with data protection, no sensitive or confidential information should be shared with any GenAI tools, including CoPilot and Firefly.
points.gist: No sensitive or confidential information should be shared with any GenAI tools, including CoPilot and Firefly.

points.quote: Before starting work on any piece of assessed work, please explore and complete our interactive guide to safe and responsible Generative AI use.
points.gist: Before starting any assessed work, explore and complete the interactive guide to safe and responsible GenAI use.

points.quote: Using GenAI to generate work that is submitted for assessment without any acknowledgement and against any directives from tutors, is a form of malpractice.
points.anchor: Health warning: academic regulations and GenAI
points.gist: Submitting GenAI-generated work without acknowledgement and against tutor directives is a form of malpractice.

points.quote: Where it is suspected that GenAI has been used when it shouldn’t have, or it has not been credited through appropriate referencing, the standard University academic malpractice procedures will apply.
points.anchor: Health warning: academic regulations and GenAI
points.gist: Suspected improper or uncredited GenAI use is dealt with under the standard academic malpractice procedures.

points.quote: There may be legitimate uses of generative AI in your subject area that are outlined on your module assessment brief or that you can discuss with your tutors.
points.anchor: Health warning: academic regulations and GenAI
points.gist: Legitimate GenAI uses may be set out in the module assessment brief or discussed with tutors.

points.quote: As of the 31 July 2025, Cite them Right guidance is that acknowledging and referencing Gen AI outputs will depend on whether that content is publicly or privately available.
points.gist: Cite them Right guidance from 31 July 2025 says how to reference GenAI output depends on whether it is public or private.

points.quote: If generative AI outputs are only available to an individual, then they are regarded as a form of "personal communication".
points.gist: GenAI outputs available only to an individual are regarded as personal communication.

points.quote: However, these tools should not be used to translate entire paragraphs or full assignments. Students should be transparent about any use of AI or translation tools and are strongly advised to consult tutors before using them.
points.anchor: Can I use GenAI as a translation tool?
points.gist: Translation tools should not translate entire paragraphs or full assignments; students should be transparent about use and consult tutors first.

points.quote: Tutors with concerns about potential malpractice may require students to share their original drafts and notes to demonstrate their own working process.
points.anchor: Can I use GenAI as a translation tool?
points.gist: Tutors with malpractice concerns may require students to share original drafts and notes to show their working process.

points.quote: Students should also avoid recording lessons or discussions without explicit permission.
points.anchor: Can I use GenAI as a translation tool?
points.gist: Students should avoid recording lessons or discussions without explicit permission.

points.quote: Information and references provided can be wrong or made up, with different sources reporting accuracy rates of between 40 to 60%.
points.anchor: Where is the information coming from and is it reliable?
points.gist: Information and references from GenAI can be wrong or made up, with sources reporting accuracy of 40 to 60%.

points.quote: GenAI tools do not have access to subscription resources so are generally searching information available on the web.
points.anchor: Where is the information coming from and is it reliable?
points.gist: GenAI tools cannot access subscription resources and generally search information available on the web.

points.quote: GenAI tools often keep copies of materials and might even use those materials for further training.
points.gist: GenAI tools often keep copies of materials and might use them for further training.

points.quote: Environmental impact: Some AI companies are not transparent about how much energy and water their training processes and tools consume so researchers and journalists are left to guestimate what this is likely to be.
points.gist: Some AI companies are not transparent about energy and water use, so researchers and journalists must estimate it.
